name: Issachar
overview: Issachar was a male member of the tribe of Levi, identified specifically as the seventh-born son of Obed-edom. Beyond this familial detail, Scripture does not provide additional personal notes about him. His position within the Levitical lineage situates him in a priestly context in Israel's history.
namesAndTitles: The name Issachar means 'there is reward,' reflecting a meaningful Hebrew designation rather than a divine bestowal. This name highlights a concept of recompense or blessing associated with his identity.
familyAndRelationships: Issachar is explicitly recorded as the son of Obed-edom, establishing his direct paternal relationship. Scripture does not mention other family connections beyond this.
scriptureSignificance: Issachar's significance lies in his place within the Levitical family, as the seventh son of Obed-edom, a notable figure in the service of the tabernacle. While the broader tribe of Issachar is recognized for wisdom and understanding in discerning the times, this particular Issachar's role is framed by his Levitical heritage. His name's meaning points to the theme of divine reward, consistent with God's faithfulness to His covenant people.
